Subject: Post-call: Performance / SLO qualification for Acme - next steps

Hi Sara / Mike —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to validate that Redwood can meet Acme's latency and throughput SLOs for the new Recommendations API:

Summary of SLO targets you gave:
- P95 latency (inference, end-to-end): <= 250ms for single-user streaming use cases
- Sustained throughput: ~12k requests/minute during peak windows (~200 req/sec)
- Concurrency target: support up to 150 concurrent long-lived streaming sessions
- Availability / failover: <1% request error budget per month; automatic fallback to smaller model variant if capacity constrained

Initial cost/performance levers we discussed to hit these SLOs:
- Continuous batching (micro-batching based on short hold windows) for throughput efficiency
- KV / prefix caching for repeated contexts to reduce per-token compute
- Quantization profiles for model variants to trade quality vs latency (8-bit, 4-bit candidates)
- Serving model variants (full-large vs medium-quant) routed by latency/cost policy

Action items I suggest:
1) You share the spreadsheet with exact traffic shape by minute/hour (attachment: acme_slo_requirements.xlsx) — you said you'd export next week.
2) Aditya will propose a short perf test plan (benchmarks + streaming test harness) and a sample config for batching/caching to validate 250ms P95 at target concurrency.
3) Priyom will sketch a cost estimate for a few profile options (dedicated pool vs hosted with reserved burst).
4) Schedule a 60-min perf sync next Wed where we walk the test results and choose which quant/model variant to pilot.

I attached our SLO playbook for reference (redwood_slo_playbook.pdf). Let me know if I missed anything.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is great, appreciate the clear summary. A couple clarifications from our side after syncing with infra team:

- The 12k req/min peak is an average across a cluster of 6 app nodes; per-node traffic will be ~2k req/min. However spikes can hit 5k req/min for a few minutes during campaigns.
- Streaming sessions are mostly text->text low-token (responses avg 30 tokens), but we need end-to-end streaming start latency (time to first token) to be <150ms for interactive flows. Total completion time can be higher.
- We currently do not want aggressive quantized outputs for ranking models that feed downstream business metrics; for that route we'd prefer higher quality medium-large models. For chat/assistant flows we can consider 8-bit or 4-bit if latency gains are meaningful.

I'll upload the traffic shape and sample traces to the spreadsheet and share by Monday. Can Aditya propose a test that includes: a streaming first-token latency test, repeated-context cache test, and a long-tail spike (burst) test?

Sara
Lead Product Manager, Acme Corp

Sara — thanks for the notes. High-level on the perf test plan and what we'll measure:

Planned test components:
1) Streaming-first-token latency: emulate your client network + model pipeline; measure TTF1 (time to first token) at P50/P95/P99 for 100, 500, 1500 concurrent sessions. Goal: demonstrate P95 < 150ms for P50/steady loads and understand degradation at P99.
2) Throughput/backpressure: sustained ramp to 200 req/s per cluster node, with short spikes to 600 req/s (to match your campaign spikes) while exercising continuous batching. We will vary the batching hold window (5ms, 10ms, 25ms) to quantify latency vs throughput trade-offs.
3) KV / prefix cache test: repeated-contexts with high cache hit rates (70-90%) vs cold runs to show per-token CPU/GPU savings and latency improvements.
4) Model-variant comparison: run the same workload across full-large (fp16), 8-bit quant, and 4-bit quant variants to measure quality (BLEU/LM/metric you provide) vs latency/cost.

Cost/perf levers we'll tune and report (so you can pick):
- Continuous batching settings (hold window, max batch size)
- Cache TTL and sharding (hot vs warm keys)
- Quantization profile and mixed-precision fallbacks
- Routing policy: route 10-20% traffic to medium-quant variant as a canary for quality checks
- Reserved dedicated pool sizing vs hosted autoscale config for burst economics

Expected deliverables:
- Test harness + scripts you can run (or we run in a controlled VPC)
- CSV of latency percentiles, tail behavior, batch sizes, and cost estimate per 1M requests for each profile
- Recommendation table: model variant vs latency vs cost with suggested rollout policy

Priyom — can you draft two cost scenarios (Dedicated 4x A100-equivalent pool + cache layer vs Hosted reserved burst) and include estimated $/1M requests for the three model variants? I can run the perf harness once we have the traffic sheet.

If that plan looks good, I'll send a calendar invite for Wed 18 Feb 09:00 PT to review initial results.

Thanks,
Aditya
